text:
Marathon Petroleum's stock has fallen 2.6% today and 8.3% over two weeks as the refinery sector unwinds from what analysts are calling the end of a major profit cycle. The trigger appears to be a broad reassessment: on November 23rd, reporting noted that "the epic boom in refinery-related stocks is unwinding," suggesting investors are rotating out of energy refining plays that had benefited from high margins. While U.S. oil prices remain elevated at $89.53 per barrel and refineries are running at 95.7% capacity, the momentum shift away from the sector is overriding those fundamentals.

The geopolitical tensions in the Middle East—Iranian mines damaging tankers in the Strait of Hormuz, Houthi attacks on Saudi refineries, and escalating U.S. sanctions on Iran—would normally support oil prices and refinery profits. Instead, the sell-off suggests the market is pricing in a longer-term view: climate negotiations collapsing on fossil fuels, combined with the sense that the exceptional refining margins of the past period are unlikely to persist, is prompting investors to exit the trade regardless of near-term supply disruptions.
